exercise.name: Stationary Bike
library_steps: Set the seat height so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom.
Pedal at a steady pace with enough resistance to breathe harder.
Lower the resistance and pedal easy for the last few minutes.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated on the bike, trunk leaning ~20 deg forward, hands on the bar. Picture 1: left pedal at the top, right at the bottom; picture 2: half a turn later, the other way round.

setup.target: Saddle height so the knee is bent ~25-35 deg at the bottom of the stroke.
Leaning forward ~15-20 deg to the bar.

muscles.role: Library primary 'cardio' has no mask; front thigh lit as the main pedalling muscle (library secondary).

muscles.emg: Gluteus maximus active in the down-stroke (S1).
Active through the bottom and back of the stroke (S1).
Gastrocnemius/soleus transfer force at the ankle (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knee bent well over 35 deg at the bottom.

sources.citation: Hug F, Dorel S. Electromyographic analysis of pedaling: a review. J Electromyogr Kinesiol. 2009;19(2):182-198.
sources.what_it_gave: Pedalling EMG: vastii and gluteus maximus drive the down-stroke, hamstrings the bottom/back, gastrocnemius transfers force at the ankle.

sources.citation: Bini R, Hume PA, Croft JL. Effects of bicycle saddle height on knee injury risk and cycling performance. Sports Med. 2011;41(6):463-476.
sources.what_it_gave: Saddle set so the knee is bent ~25-35 deg at the bottom of the pedal stroke.

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
